Q: This python code to detect ellipse detects more ellipse than the present ellipse A:

Here is one approach in Python OpenCV.

If you use contours, it will produce double contours for each band, one outside and one inside. So use connected components to extract each band.

  • Read the input

  • Convert to grayscale

  • Threshold

  • Use connectedComponentsWithStats to label each elliptical band in the threshold image

  • Loop over each index in the number of labels. Filter out any small regions. Then get each labeled band. Then get the x,y coordinates of each white pixel in the band. Fit an ellipse to bands with 5 or more points. Draw each ellipse as red on a copy of the input image. Print ellipse centers and diameters.

  • Save images

Input:

import cv2
import numpy as np

# read the input
img = cv2.imread('circles6.png')

# convert to grayscale
gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

# threshold and invert
thresh = cv2.threshold(gray, 128, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY)[1]
thresh = 255 - thresh

# do connected components on skeleton image to numerically label each one
# note: cntours produce double the number of contours (outside and inside)
# for the labels, the background is zero and skeletons are 1,2...6
num_labels, labels, stats, centroids = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(thresh)

# create result image as copy of input for drawing ellipses
result = img.copy()

# loop over each label (skip 0 as it is background)
for i in range(1, num_labels):

    # get area from stats
    area = stats[i, cv2.CC_STAT_AREA]
    
    # filter out any small specks in the image that have been labeled
    if area < 100:
        continue
    
    # extract a single skeleton from the label and make a binary image
    # note: labels == i makes a true/false image for label i
    # then astype converts to 0 or 1 and 255 converts to 0 or 255
    single_band = (labels == i).astype(np.uint8) * 255

    # get points y,x from the single_skeleton
    y, x = np.where(single_band > 0)
    points = np.column_stack((x, y))

    # be sure we have enough points to fit an ellipse (need at least 5)
    if len(points) < 5:
        continue
    
    # fit the ellipse
    ellipse = cv2.fitEllipse(points)
    (xc,yc),(d1,d2),angle = ellipse

    # print rounded ellipse values
    print(f"index: {i}  center: ({xc+0.5:.0f}, {yc+0.5:.0f})  diameters: ({d1+0.5:.0f}, {d2+0.5:.0f})")

    # draw ellipse
    cv2.ellipse(result, ellipse, (0, 0, 255), 5)

# save images
cv2.imwrite('circles6_thresh.jpg', thresh)
cv2.imwrite('circles6_ellipses.jpg', result)


# show images
cv2.imshow('thresh', thresh)
cv2.imshow('ellipses', result)
cv2.waitKey(0)

Q: realtime app need push service advice A:

2026 update on how I would approach this with PubNub.

For your 100-truck case, you do not need one subscribe connection per truck. PubNub can multiplex subscriptions to multiple channels over the same subscribe connection. The client may use another socket for non-subscribe operations, so I would not think about it as "one socket for everything."

https://www.pubnub.com/docs/general/channels/subscribe

You also don't create channels in advance. A channel is created when you first publish to it.

https://www.pubnub.com/docs/general/channels/overview

For a smaller number of channels, you can just multiplex them. PubNub recommends around 10-50 channels per subscribe request. The limits documentation advertises 100 channels as the hard limit for multiplexing, although the server itself doesn't have a channel-count limit. In practice, URI length is also something you need to consider.

https://www.pubnub.com/docs/general/setup/limits#subscribe

For exactly 100 truck channels, I would not push a 100-item channel list to the edge. Better use a channel group, or wildcard subscribe if your channel naming works for it.

For wildcard subscriptions, use dot-separated channel names, for example trucks.34 and subscribe to trucks.*. The wildcard has to end in .*, and you cannot publish directly to a wildcard pattern. Wildcard subscriptions and channel groups require the Stream Controller add-on. Normal multiplexing works without it.

One more important thing if you are using PHP. PubNub's PHP subscribe call blocks execution, so subscription code should normally run in a long-lived worker/process rather than inside a normal PHP web request:

https://www.pubnub.com/docs/sdks/php/api-reference/publish-and-subscribe

Disclosure: I work for PubNub.

Q: MaterializeCSS datepicker: setDate does not update the view A:

My friend, you have found a bug in MaterializeCSS version v1.0.0-rc.2!

I can suggest you my workaround: call instance._finishSelection() after calling instance.setDate() to see your changes.

I've created a small JSFiddle to test this workaround:

https://jsfiddle.net/tfbajzk0/

Update 2026: the bug is still there, as the repository has not received a commit since Jun 1, 2020 and at the time of writing has 164 opened merge requests. So I recommend not using that software anymore.

  • https://github.com/Dogfalo/materialize/issues/6074

Q: TypeError: Failed to load plugin 'jest' declared in '.eslintrc': Class extends value undefined is not a constructor or null A:

Firstly, check your node_modules directory, and see if eslint-plugin-jest is in there.

If not, delete your package-lock.json and then run npm install.

Q: Find first match A:

The index value will be used to access other columns containing information about that particular tax code

To get the values in the column that matches, place the tax code in cell B1, the codes (D0, D1, NT, L, K) in row C1:G1, the data in C2:G, and use filter() in cell A1 to get a whole column:

=filter(C1:G, search(C1:G1, B1))

In the event a code may match several tax codes, and you only want the first result, add index():

=index(filter(C1:G, search(C1:G1, B1)),, 1)

These formulas will return the whole column, including the code that matched. To only get the data, use C2:G.

See filter(), search() and index().

Q: Python App for Lenel S2 NetBox API is limited on results A:

As you have observered, the API gives limited responses.
This is common for APIs with the potential to handle large amounts of data.

Q: Getting WebView2 Assembly load errors when calling Add-Type. Is it my code or the assembly? A:

The issue is due to an assembly conflict on System.Runtime, your package is trying to load 4.2.1.0 and PowerShell 5.1 already uses 4.0.0.0.

Try downloading the dlls directly from NuGet, this process has worked for me in PSVersion 5.1.26100.9168:

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

try {
    $uri = 'https://www.nuget.org/api/v2/package/Microsoft.Web.WebView2'
    $req = Invoke-WebRequest $uri -UseBasicParsing
    $zip = [System.IO.Compression.ZipArchive]::new($req.RawContentStream)
    $dir = mkdir .\WebView2
    $zip.Entries | Where-Object FullName -Like lib/net462/*.dll | ForEach-Object {
        $dest = Join-Path $dir.FullName $_.Name
        [System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::ExtractToFile($_, $dest)
    }

    Add-Type -Path .\WebView2\*.dll
}
finally {
    if ($zip) { $zip.Dispose() }
}

The code above will download the needed dlls and store them in the WebView2 folder in your current location, then load them. If all went well, then you should get the expected output:

True     False    WebView2                  System.Windows.Forms.Control
